Hi Samira — really glad the demo was useful. Looping in David (networking/runtime) and Irene (security/compliance) to propose a short baseline and next steps.

Short answer up front: we can support both IP-based allowlisting and FQDN-based controls. For the POC we typically provide a small set of stable egress addresses (ephemeral lease model) and also publish canonical FQDNs for our control-plane endpoints. Runtime model choices affect the exposure surface:

- Control plane (management, metrics, callbacks): we ask customers to allow a small set of outbound FQDNs and the accompanying short list of leased egress IPs. These flows should be routed through the perimeter and have strict logging.
- Runtime (inference requests to and from model servers): we recommend letting runtime egress use a dedicated NAT pool that preserves source IP where possible (some customers require source IP for auditing). If source-ip preservation is required we can discuss using a NAT that maps to a per-subnet fixed IP or deploying an on-prem egress proxy controlled by NetOps.

I attached a quick starter pack (glb-egress-ip-matrix.xlsx) that lists the canonical hostnames, SNI patterns, and our recommended firewall rules. Also attached is a short readme with TTL and rotation cadence.

Proposed next steps (30-minute sync):
- David and Samira to confirm whether Greenleaf needs source-IP preservation for runtime calls (action owner: Greenleaf, due: Tue Oct 5)
- NetOps to share initial FQDN and internal approval SLA (owner: NetOps, due: Tue Oct 5)
- Redwood to provide final leased IPs and rotation cadence for control plane (owner: Avery/David, deliverable: egress-ip-matrix)

If that works I'll schedule a slot Monday to align on the NAT/proxy pattern and firewall ticket wording.

Samira — quick technical clarifications from my side to make sure NetOps has what they need when they open the firewall ticket: 

1) Source IP preservation: if you need to see the original client IP on our runtime, we recommend one of the following (ranked by simplicity -> control):
   - NAT mapping per-subnet: customers allocate a small fixed NAT block and map subnets to consistent egress IPs (we surface the mapping in our telemetry).
   - On-prem egress proxy: you run a proxy (Envoy/squid) that forwards to Redwood control plane; proxy preserves client headers and gives you full audit control.
   - Mutual TLS with client certs for runtime health callbacks (if you require mTLS instead of IP-based allowlists).

2) DNS/FQDN behavior: we publish these hostnames: api.private.redwood.com (control plane), telemetry.private.redwood.com (metrics, optional), and runtime.egress.redwood.net (if you opt into our managed NAT pool). For FQDN rules please allow both A and AAAA lookups and a 5-10 minute TTL. We rotate leased NAT addresses every 14 days by default for POCs but can extend to 30 days for enterprise contracts.

3) TLS/SNI: We rely on standard TLS 1.2/1.3. There are no proprietary ALPNs. SNI will be present for api.private.redwood.com. We do not currently support TLS client fingerprint pinning for outbound egress. If you have DPI rules that look for SNI, allow api.private.redwood.com and runtime.egress.redwood.net.

I can join the call Monday. If NetOps can provide their firewall ticket template I can pre-fill the required fields.

-David
